text:
Sasha: FYI seeing a host-side tail latency uptick on streaming after the kernel-affinity rollout. p95 +55ms on small payloads. Starts ~08:12UTC when rollout hit prod.

Raj: which frontends? grpc, http2, or both? quick perf counters?

Sasha: predominantly HTTP/2. GRPC looks okay. Captured a smoke trace: `./bin/stream-replay --rate 500 --frames small` (will attach). Kernel selector log shows repeated picks of `kernel_throughput_v2` for sequences < 100 tokens; that seems wrong.

Elaine: we bumped min_batch_ms from 2->6 in the batching heuristics yesterday to reduce ops. That can increase batching at the ingress, but for tiny frames it may cause extra buffering + more writev scatter. Also recall we flipped `coalesce_on_write` to false in the proxy for a micro-optim.

Mike: `perf record` + `perf script` showed syscall hotpath: `epoll_wait` wakeups + `writev` with many iovecs. Hot functions: `tokenizer::emit`, `proxy::frame_writer`, `kvcache::lookup_slowpath`.

Sasha: kvcache spikes correlate with write bursts. Samples: `kvcache.hits=22%`, `evictions/sec=420` during a 60s window. When coalesce_on_write=true on canary host, hits jump to 89% and p95 drops ~60ms.

Raj: Interesting. Could be that small fragmented writes are causing many distinct key accesses before the KV prefetch/pipeline can prime. Prefetch was gated by the chunker hint bits. Did the chunker change the frag size distribution?

Elaine: yes — chunker now emits more micro-fragments to reduce buffering latency on large streams. But for short requests that backfires. My suggestion: add a fast-path in kernel selector that prefers `kernel_latency_v1` when avg_frame_size <= 80B OR frag_count > 8. Also revert coalesce_on_write toggle or make it adaptive: enable coalescing when avg_iovecs > 4.

Sasha: I pushed branch `opt/small-frame-adaptive-coalesce` with:
- kernel selector threshold change: frame_threshold = 80
- adaptive coalesce: coalesce_on_write = avg_iovecs > 4
- re-enable kvcache prefetch for frag_hint <=2

ci-bot: ci/build 1289 passed :white_check_mark: https://ci.internal/1289

Mike: Can we get a flamegraph link? also capture socket-level traces (sendmsg/writev counts).

Sasha: uploaded traces: https://artifacts/replays/1810007777/frames.json and flamegraphs at https://perf.internal/fg/1810007777. Quick excerpt from frames.json: `frame_sizes_histogram: [<=32B:34%, 33-64B:28%, 65-128B:22%, >128B:16%]`, `avg_iovecs=6.8`.

Raj: That histogram definitely favours the adaptive coalesce rule. Next step: ablation experiment: enable selector tweak only vs coalesce only vs both. Can you spin 3 canaries?

Elaine: I'll coordinate canaries. Also propose adding a telemetry metric `ingress.small_frame_ratio` and tag selector decisions with `decision_kernel` so Optimize can recommend changes automatically.

Mike: If coalescing helps we should also look at gRPC SETTINGS windowing. HTTP/2 SETTINGS ACK churn was visible — maybe clients are aggressively toggling SETTINGS on reconnects leading to more HEADERS frames. Valve idea: temporarily increase SETTINGS coalescing window to 50ms for chosen routes.

Sasha: canary results (10m runs):
- selector-only: p95 -12ms, kvcache hits 41%
- coalesce-only: p95 -52ms, kvcache hits 87%
- both: p95 -60ms, kvcache hits 91%

Raj: looks like coalescing is the big win; selector tweak gives additional polish. Any regressions on large-batch workflows?

Sasha: ran large-batch test (batch_size=64, seq=512): no degradations within noise. `throughput_v2` still chosen for long sequences. Good.

Elaine: plan: (1) roll both fixes to prod canaries, (2) add telemetry + selector tagging, (3) follow-up Optimize rule to detect high small_frame_ratio and suggest coalescing + client hints, (4) doc the kernel-affinity knobs. I'll open PRs for telemetry and docs.

ci-bot: deploy/canary 2024-06-19T09:10:00Z started :rocket:

Mike: +1. Also add a small unit test for selector histogram binning so future chunker changes don't regress decisions.

Sasha: will post final perf diff and flamegraphs once canary has 30m of steady-state. Ping me for early access to the canary endpoint. :pray:
